title: Yield-curve recession clock
hypothesis: The live book's maximum drawdown is still about -46.8%, with the trough on 2009-03-09. Sleeve-exit rules (the credit-spread hedge, the volatility scale, the multi-lookback vote, the trailing-peak stop, and the N-day band confirmation) left that trough in place, because by then the UPRO sleeve is already in T-bills and the loss that remains is the SPY half. Parking part of that half in T-bills whenever the 200-day band is off did cut the drawdown, and it was rejected: the cash stake ran through every off-trend episode, including the rebounds that are not recessions, and the CAGR give-up was larger than the bar allows. This test does not key off the equity trend. The trigger is the Treasury curve. The spread is the 10-year yield minus the 13-week bill yield, both in percent as Yahoo quotes ^TNX and ^IRX. Equity damage after an inversion has historically arrived as the curve later re-steepens, so the rule is not cash while the spread is negative. A session starts the clock when the spread crosses from at or above a depth to strictly below it. title: Two-sided UPRO drift band
hypothesis:
The live book resets both piles to 50/50 on a quarterly calendar. Between those dates the sleeve is 3x while the trend is on, so a rally lifts its weight above one half and a drop pushes it below. The calendar also trades when the gap is small. The original grid compared monthly and quarterly calendars. The 2026-11-13 exposure run then scored daily, monthly, and quarterly on this same 50/50 book; the walk-forward pick was the daily reset and it missed the materiality bar. The 2026-10-31 test required N closes through the 200-day band before the sleeve flipped, and the 2% band itself is already the live filter, so this test does not rescore hysteresis. The 2026-11-04 test replaced the calendar with a one-sided ceiling: it sold UPRO only after the weight was above half, and it left a shrunken sleeve alone. The walk-forward kept the calendar in every year. That rule dropped the side the calendar still does, which is buying the sleeve back after UPRO has fallen and the book is under its 2x budget while the trend is on. This test does not add a regime signal and does not sell the core. It replaces the quarterly mix date with a two-sided band. After the close, if the sleeve is in UPRO and its weight is strictly more than a fixed band away from one half, in either direction, the next open resets both piles to 50/50. If the gap is inside the band, or the sleeve is in T-bills, the piles are left alone. A trend flip still swaps the sleeve instrument and does not by itself resize the piles. The three-down-close dip is unchanged. Bands are 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 percentage points, fixed before this sample is scored. The quarterly calendar is the current book, already counted, and is the walk-forward's option to keep it. Its name sorts first, so a tie in the trailing excess Sharpe keeps it. The five bands are new trials. Fills stay next-open with 5 bp one-way costs. Cash pays no spread. The study counts, on the live book and before any new cell is scored, how far the UPRO weight sits from one half. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.

title: Credit-regime gate on the UPRO sleeve
hypothesis:
The live sleeve stays at 3x until SPY closes through the 200-day 2% band. That lag is why the book's out-of-sample max drawdown is still about -46.8%. The 2026-10-25 test, re-scored on 2026-10-26, moved the sleeve to T-bills when the 20-session change in the Baa spread exceeded 10, 20, 35, or 50 basis points. That spike rule did not move the out-of-sample drawdown. This test does not rescore it, those thresholds, or the FRED series. It also does not rescore holding IEF, LQD, or HYG. Those ETFs are not positions. The signal is the relative total return of credit versus the intermediate Treasury, known at the close. At each SPY session, HYG, LQD, and IEF contribute their last adjusted close dated on or before that session. The primary ratio is HYG divided by IEF once that ratio has a full simple average of W sessions. Until then the ratio is LQD divided by IEF, once that average exists. Before either average exists the gate does not block the sleeve. When the active ratio changes, the state is set from that close alone: a close above the upper band is healthy, a close below the lower band is stress, and a close inside the band does not block. After that, stress turns on at the first close below the average times (1 - B) and turns off at the first close above the average times (1 + B). Inside the band the previous state is kept. Stress moves only the UPRO sleeve to T-bills on the next open. The SPY core, the three-down-close dip, and the quarterly mix are unchanged. W is 100, 150, or 200. B is 0 or 0.02. Those six cells were fixed before this sample was scored. The walk-forward may also keep the current book. That cell is already counted, and its name sorts first, so a tie in the trailing excess Sharpe keeps it. Fills stay next-open with 5 bp one-way costs. Cash pays no spread. The stitched path is kept only when it clears the materiality bar.
